column1: # basic/spec/control.tsv — the control-flow words' parity corpus.
# Same notation as stack.tsv, plus BRACKETS: a `[ … ]` run in the program
# column assembles into a LIST value. The corpus has no parser behind it,
# so the brackets are the only way to write a code body.
# Only `do` is covered. `if`, `case` and `for` are not ported to basic/ts
# yet — their runtime halves are entangled with their analysis halves, and
# core/ts has no carrier lattice (design/GO-TS-PARITY.0.md). Rows for them
# would encode a gap as a contract.
# --- do: runs the body, returns its ENTIRE residual ------------------------
do [ 1 ]

column3: the WHOLE residual, not just the last value

column1: # `do [ ]` is DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Under this corpus's minimal fixture
# registry it yields the empty list itself (`[]`), while the full `boru`
# binary yields nothing at all — `print (do [])` raises no_value_error.
# That difference is between two REGISTRIES, not between the two engines,
# so it is not a parity row, and encoding either answer here would pin a
# fixture artifact as a language contract. Open question, worth chasing
# before `do`'s analysis half lands.
do [ 1 2 swap ]
column3: the body sees the word vocabulary

column1: do [ 1 dup ]
do [ do [ 1 ] ]
column3: a nested body's residual flows out

column1: do [ 1 do [ 2 ] ]
# A body error becomes an Error VALUE rather than propagating — that is the
# word's whole point, and why the handler returns instead of re-raising.
do [ nosuchword ]
column3: an error in the body is caught and returned as a value

column1: do [ 1 nosuchword ]
column3: the caught error REPLACES the residual, it does not join it

column1: do [ 1 5 pick ]
column2: error(pick: index 5 out of range (stack depth 1))
column3: the escape hatch catches UNCODED errors too, not just boru ones

column1: do List
column3: a bare type literal fails to MATCH — dispatch refuses before the handler
